recipes.name: Lobster Bisque
ingredients_raw: 1 pound cooked and cubed lobster meat

steps.text: In a small frying pan place 1/4 cup chicken broth and the onion. Cook over a low heat for 5 to 7 minutes.
In a medium size pot over medium heat melt the butter. Slowly whisk in flour. Whisk until a creamy mixture is created.

Gradually pour in broth, whisking constantly. Whisk in milk, salt, onion, lobster meat, Worcestershire sauce and cayenne pepper. Heat until soup is almost boiling. Do not boil the soup as the milk will curdle when boiled.

review.reviewBody: Okay... this recipe was very good, but there were a few adjustments that I had to make. I went ahead and followed the directions, but instead of using milk, I substituted it with heavy whipping cream. I chopped the onions, instead of slicing them. I also added a few tablespoons of tomato puree, I added some more worestshire sauce and some more chayenne pepper and VIOLA! The recipe was perfected. Oh... I also let it cook on low heat for about 1 hour. The trick to this recipe is to allow it to simmer. Wilma, you had the right idea, but you just needed a little more special additions to your recipe to make it perfect. Thank you for giving me the basics. This has become one of my family's favorite! Michi in Miami

I followed the reviews and used beer to steam the lobster and use as a soup base, cooking the empty shells and a celery stalk int the left over beer for an hour. 
It was AMAZING. 
I added four cups of chicken stock to the beer along with 1 sautéed onion, 6 stalks of celery & 8 cloves of garlic. I pureed half of the that and added it to the soup base along with three Tbs. of tomato paste and a dash of Old Bay seasoning . Like others, I doubled the flour and Worcestershire sauce to the base. Cooked for an hour before adding 1 and 1/2 cups half and half and simmered another half hour. Added the lobster just before serving. Really awesome!! Everyone said it was a 5 star course that would pay for - will make this again for sure.

I had some scallops that I needed to cook, and I saw this recipe and thought it would work, and I had all the ingredients on hand. I made the recipe mostly according to the suggestions in the video (double butter, flower, more Worcestershire, and sherry). Changes I made, besides the scallops: 
 Instead of opening a quart box of stock/broth, I used a cup of water and a teaspoon of Better than Bouillon. I used gluten-free flour and it worked fine. After removing the onions from the broth, I chopped them before adding. In retrospect, even though I cooked the onions about 7 minutes, I think I should have cooked them a bit longer, as they still were a little crunchy. Overall, this was delicious. If I make it again, I might try a little Hungarian paprika.

I hate when people rate a recipe but then totally make it their own....but here I am. So I doubled the recipe and instead of 4 slices of onion I used 2 small whole onions sliced and cooked in about a cup of broth. Instead of using all milk I used 3 cups of milk and one small carton of whipping cream. I puréed a can of stewed tomatoes and puréed the onion slices that were cooked in the broth and added that to the broth prior to the milk. I upped the cayenne to about 3/4 teaspoon and added about 2 tsp of onion salt. After all my changes, it as amazing.

We live in Texas so as soon as the temperature drops down into the sixties, we think it’s time to break out all the fixins’ for chili. But instead I made the Lobster bisque today. I followed the recipe only I used shallots instead of onions, gave them a rough chop, doubled the cayenne, used a half cup of half and half, half cup of milk and a full cup of heavy cream and added just a little garlic. The recipe turned out with perfect texture and was absolutely delicious. I served it with Fontina and Gruyere grilled cheese sandwiches. This is a keeper for another cold night here in Texas.

this was super easy and the quickest/easiest bisque I've ever made but I had a lot of substitutions. 1) Seafood broth for chicken, 2) more onion, I used a whole one 3) Tomato paste for Flour, also adds pink 4) added sherry to taste, 5) used 1/2 and 1/2 6) used small lobster langoustinos find at Trader Joes and blended in about a 1/3 of broth to make it thicker/creamier, left. I doubled recipe for a party and got rave reviews from everyone! I think the suggestion to add garlic is also good.

Very good. I still need to tweak. First of all I needed to make it gluten free... I used sorghum flour and a pinch of xanthan gum. Seemed to work well. Next I added about 3/4 c. rendered sherry, tripled the butter and used half-and-half instead of milk. Only about 14 oz lobster meat. Tried to emulsify with an immersion blender but the meat resisted a great deal. Next time I will add more worcestershire... I did add a little extra cayenne and salt and that punched it up some, but I think it can get better.

This is a four star recipe as written and 5 star with adding 1/8 cup sherry, 2tbsp tomato paste, 1/2 tsp black pepper, and replace milk with half and half. Restaurant quality! The flour amount called for was perfect. The people who complained it wasn’t, most likely did not bring the soup to an almost boil for it to thicken up. I added the cooked langostino lobster the last 5 minutes of cooking, lowered to lowest heat setting after soup was thick enough in order to not over cook/toughen the lobster. Thank you for the great start to a perfect lobster bisque.

This was good as it but I did alter the recipe. For my notes, I simmered the cooked lobster tails, then with leftover steam water and shells , added g. onion, celery seed, sage branch, in half & half for about an hour. Strain pot. Melt butter, add onion till brown, then add flour. Then whisk in seasoned milk, stock, cayenne, 3 T tomato paste, worst sauce. Simmer 10-20 add paprika and chopped lobster. Turned out great!

Loved this, it was super easy! I pretty much stuck to the recipe but did add some cornstarch in chicken broth to thicken up a bit at the end. Next time I’m going to replace some of the chicken stock with cooking sherry added at the end for a smooth finish. I like that milk was used rather than heavy cream and I did use low-fat milk.

I read the reviews and added tomato paste, old bay seasoning, Epicure herb & garlic seasoning to taste. I used spot prawns instead of lobster. I chopped them into small pieces and added them to the bisque uncooked. I let it simmer on low for one hour. Added chives at the time of serving. I will definitely make this again. Was even better the next day.

Think creamy like, tomato soup. My 1st try... I added potatoes for a thickener, chopped celery for flavor, and tomato puree for color & flavor. Not good. My 2nd try... I removed all the lobster, then used the immersion blender. The base was creamy & delicious. I returned the lobster to the base. Follow the directions that Wilma Scott gave you.
I loved this recipe. I used seafood stock instead of chicken stock. I also used 2 cups of heavy cream. This is a great recipe.
I used a tomato base with a crab stock with finely diced vegetable trio and diced cooked 16 ounce lobster taps . It turned out delicious!
Didn’t quite have enough lobster, so I added some diced up shrimp, and some diced up crab. Was still amazing.

Great recipe. Easy to male! I tweaked it to reflect my spicy attitude and decreased the salt content by using a PINCH of salt then using garlic powder and crushed red pepper when the recipe called for salt.
Tastes great. Will add more flour to make it thicker next time.
I took everybody's advice on using cream rather than milk, adding tomato paste, and doubled on seasonings... it was delicious!
Simple and amazing! Hard to say that about any recipe! I also used one cup of whole milk and one cup of cream. Added diced potatoes and corn. Deelish!
